gloss: to persist in; to insist on; to stick stubbornly to

definitions.gloss: to persist in; to insist on; to stick stubbornly to
definitions.explanation: To refuse to change one's opinion, position, or method despite pressure or reason to do so. Implies stubbornness and inflexibility.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{意見|いけん}に{固執|こしつ}する。
examples.english: To insist on one's own opinion.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}いやり{方|かた}に{固執|こしつ}していては{進歩|しんぽ}がない。
examples.english: There's no progress if you cling to the old way of doing things.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{立場|たちば}に{固執|こしつ}して、{誰|だれ}の{話|はなし}も{聞|き}こうとしなかった。
examples.english: He stubbornly stuck to his position and refused to listen to anyone.

notes:
A する verb meaning to stubbornly persist in or cling to something. Composed of {固|こ} (solid, firm) + {執|しつ} (hold, grasp). Always negative in connotation, implying that the person is unreasonably rigid.

PRONUNCIATION:
Also read こしゅう, though こしつ is more standard in modern usage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {意見|いけん}に{固執|こしつ}する: to insist on one's opinion
- {立場|たちば}に{固執|こしつ}する: to cling to one's position
- {方法|ほうほう}に{固執|こしつ}する: to stick stubbornly to a method
- {前例|ぜんれい}に{固執|こしつ}する: to cling to precedent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {執着|しゅうちゃく}する: to be attached to, to be obsessed with — broader, includes emotional attachment to things or people
- こだわる: to be particular about — can be positive (pursuit of quality) or negative
- {頑固|がんこ}: stubborn — an adjective describing the person's character rather than a specific action
